11 tool stack that actually runs my business day to day

Not tools I tried once. Tools I'd be stuck without tomorrow.

For building:

Cursor | my main editor now, AI-assisted coding cuts my build time in half
Claude | I use it for planning architecture before I write a line of code
v0 by Vercel | turns a rough UI idea into working React in minutes

For automation:

n8n | connects everything else on this list without me writing glue code
Zapier | for the simple stuff I don't want to think about
Make (Integromat) | for the automations too complex for Zapier

For client work:

Notion | every client, every project, one dashboard
Calendly | booking calls without the back-and-forth
Loom | I send a video instead of a meeting whenever I can

For growth:

Buffer | schedules content so I'm not posting live every day
ChatGPT | first draft on everything, then I edit in my own voice

Total monthly cost: less than one hour of my billable time.

**Chase Spenst**: Founder at Good Operator with 19 years 4 months of experience. Previous roles include Director at Alliance Brands Ltd., Co Founder at The Wheelhouse, LLC, and Director, Solutions Development at Evolent Health. Based in Los Angeles, California, United States [US].

---

Your finances and financial systems should be an asset. Not a utility or box you check.
Here's the mistakes I see most companies and accountants making:

1) Emphasize accuracy for tax filings
-> instead of relevance for decision making.
Look, of course the numbers have to be right for taxes. That's table stakes. But your books should be built for the business, not the IRS. Things need to be accurate, but more important for running the business is that information is relevant and directionally sound.

2) Stress over details like submitting receipts
-> instead of stressing over systems like the cash cycle
Again, proper documentation, compliance, etc. very important. But the focus has to be on higher impact things. Your cash cycle - getting invoices out on time, collections, tracking payables and timing the payments - can mean the difference between never having money and feeling stretched vs sitting on nice cash buffer.

3) Advise on where to save money
-> instead of advising where to spend money

results.snippet:
# You're 1 layer away from a business that runs without YOU. | Aleksandar Miljković · LinkedIn · 2026-07-24

**Aleksandar Miljković**: Co-Founder at Sawify for 1 year 5 months with 4 years 7 months of total professional experience. Previous roles include Founder at Intraise and Founder at Interaise. Based in Niš, Centralna Srbija, Serbia [RS].

---

You're 1 layer away from a business that runs without YOU.

Here's what's actually sitting below your revenue ↓

Most founders I talk to are optimizing the same 5 things:

• Revenue numbers
• Client deliverables
• Marketing content
• Sales conversations
• Team meetings

That's the visible work.
The stuff clients pay for.

But when I looked at businesses that actually scale, they all had something else, 10 invisible systems running underneath:

→ Lead qualification criteria (you stop wasting time on bad fits)
→ Onboarding sequences that run automatically (clients start without you being there)
→ Delivery templates (quality doesn't require your constant attention)
→ Quality checkpoints (nothing ships broken)
→ Communication protocols (no one's waiting on you to respond)
→ Handoff docs (your team stops asking "how do I do this?")
→ Decision frameworks (choices happen without you in every meeting)
→ SOPs that actually work (systems replace your memory)
→ Escalation logic (problems route to the right person)
→ Operating principles (the rails everything runs on)

The visible stuff creates revenue.
The invisible stuff creates leverage.

April 21, 2026 20 min

# AI Is Automating Accounting — But It's Not Replacing Accountants

Logan Graf, CPA and founder of a fully virtual accounting firm, joins Macgill Davis on what AI is changing inside accounting firms, from tax prep to pricing.

## Guest

Logan Graf

CPA & Founder, Graf Tax Co.

Logan is a CPA based in Austin, Texas who runs a fully virtual accounting firm serving business owners and individuals. He also creates content for other accountants and hosts a community for accounting firm owners. He has been a Rize user for nearly five years.

## Key Takeaways

- 1. AI is automating low-value accounting tasks like basic tax prep and data entry — but every output still needs human verification before it can be trusted
- 2. Basic tax returns are getting commoditized by AI tax prep tools, which means accounting firms focused only on simple returns will see client churn
- 3. The real value for accountants is shifting from execution to trust, relationships, and advisory — clients who want a relationship will always pay for a human
- 4. AI can process bank statements and generate trial balances, but professionals still need to verify everything — blind faith in AI output is the biggest risk
- 5. Tax-specific AI tools like BlueJ AI, CoCounsel, and TaxGPT outperform general LLMs for tax research because they are trained on authoritative tax code
